recipes.title: RECIPE FOR PANETTONE WITH CANDIED TANGERINE
recipes.docx:
To celebrate the upcoming Easter, we’d like to share with you a recipe for panettone with incredibly juicy, soft and tender crumb!

So, grab your apron and enjoy working with an incredible panettone dough with a pleasant citrus aroma of candied tangerines!

#marusya_recipe

### Candied tangerines

150–200 g tangerine peel
2 g salt
250–300 g caster sugar
1 vanilla pod
80 g rum

### Rum soaked dried fruits

60 g golden raisins
60 g dried cranberries
60 g candied tangerines
150 g rum

### Bread starter
250 g milk 3.2%
7 g caster sugar
7–8 g dry yeast
150 g strong flour

### Panettone dough
165 g whole eggs (~3 pcs)
150 g caster sugar
1 vanilla pod
lemon zest
zest of 2 oranges
415 g bread starter
400 g strong flour
2 g salt
100 g butter 82%
330 g rum soaked dried fruits

### Candied tangerines

Wash and pat dry the tangerines. Remove the peel, cut it into small pieces, place in a saucepan and pour water on top so that it completely covers the peel.
- Add 2 g of salt, bring to a boil and simmer for about 2–5 minutes. Drain the water. Repeat the same steps 2–3 more times to get rid of the bitterness of the albedo.

- Place sugar in a thick-bottomed saucepan and add water so that it covers the sugar by ~ 0.5–1.0 cm. Add vanilla seeds, rum and warm everything up until the sugar dissolves completely. Add the tangerine peels. Bring to a boil and simmer until almost all of the liquid has evaporated.
- Arrange the candied tangerine on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and dry for ~ 1–2 hours in the oven (with the oven door slightly ajar) on minimum heat.

Wash and pat dry the dried fruits, mix with candied tangerine, pour in cognac / rum / limoncello or orange juice. Leave in the fridge overnight.

### Bread starter

- Pour the warm milk into a small bowl, add sugar, dry yeast, mix until smooth and leave for 5–7 minutes until the mixture foams a little. Add the sifted flour, carefully combine with a whisk and leave in a warm place for ~ 30–60 minutes until the dough doubles in volume.
- if desired, you can replace dry yeast with 25 g of fresh yeast

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR THE PERFECT CHEESECAKE CRUMBLE
recipes.docx:
As you probably already know, I am a perfectionist by nature, and the story of creation of this recipe is closely related to this trait of mine.

Here is how it was. Once, when tasting my new cheesecake, my family, who used to be treated to nice desserts, ate the cream cheese layer with great pleasure, but left the crust almost untouched.

An irresistible desire to make tasters enjoy both the cream cheese layer and the shortbread, inspired me to create an incredibly tasty, pleasantly crunchy shortbread crumble that disappears from the plate in a matter of minutes:

- 95 g butter 82% (1)
- 80 g of icing sugar
- 18 g egg yolks (~1 pc.)
- 150 g all-purpose flour
- 10 g cornstarch
- 70 g ground hazelnuts/almonds
- 2 g rock salt
- 10-20 g butter 82% (2)
- 20-30 g coconut oil
- 10 g milk 3.2%

- Mix soft butter (1) and icing sugar until combined. Add the yolk, mix. Add flour, sifted with cornstarch, ground nuts and salt, and mix in a mixer for 30–40 seconds until crumbs have formed. It is important not to mix the dough for a long time.
- Transfer the crumbs to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, distribute them evenly and place in the freezer for at least 30 minutes. Bake in an oven, preheated to 170–180 °C, for about 15–18 minutes, then cool down completely. The well-baked shortbread crumbs should be crispy and golden brown.
- Place the crumble in a food processor or blender and process it in pulses. Add 10–20 g soft butter (2), 20–30 g coconut oil and 10 g milk, mix thoroughly.
- Grease the walls of the cake ring with coconut oil or regular butter (the bottom of the ring should be tightly covered with foil in advance). Form the base of the cheesecake by pressing the shortbread crumbs first against the sides and then — the bottom of the cake ring. Then level the crust and make it smooth using a bent tablespoon. Put in the freezer for at least 30 min.

recipes.title: COTTAGE CHEESE CASSEROLE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
UA Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko

Having tried dozens of cottage cheese casseroles, I finally found and adjusted a recipe that doesn’t fail to delight all fans of this simple yet tasty dessert since then.

In my kitchen this dessert disappears in a flash! What about yours? Let's check?

#marusya_recipe

- 50–150 g raisins (to taste)
- 1 kg cottage cheese 5–9%
- 10 g baking powder
- 2 g rock salt
- 300 g sour cream 15–25%
- 150 g semolina
- 440 g whole eggs (~8 pcs)
- 200 g of caster sugar
- 1 tsp. vanilla paste
- fresh berries for decoration

- Rinse the raisins thoroughly and place in a bowl. Pour the boiling water on top and leave for 15–20 minutes. Drain the water and pat dry the raisins.
- Place cottage cheese in a large deep bowl, add baking powder, salt and mix.
- In a separate container, combine sour cream with semolina and leave for 15–20 minutes to swell, then combine with the cottage cheese mass and mix until smooth.
- Add eggs, sugar and vanilla paste to the mixer bowl. Whip using a whisk attachment on medium–maximum speed for about 4–6 minutes until a light and fluffy mass has formed.

- The amount of sugar in the casserole can vary from 150 to 250 g: adding 150 g of sugar will ensure a slightly sweet dessert, 200 g – moderately sweet, and 250 g will result in a sweet casserole. Be guided by your taste, as well as the amount of raisins added (if any)

- Incorporate the whipped eggs into the cottage cheese mass in 2–3 lots, mixing thoroughly until smooth after each addition. Add the raisins and mix again.

Swipe the carousel to read the continuation

recipes.title: COCONUT GANACHE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
Would you like a recipe for ganache?

Today I am sharing with you a recipe for an incredibly delicious coconut ganache which can be used as a filling for your cake. It seems that the coconut smell is all around me today, so here you go

To make coconut ganache you will need:

- 120 g fresh brown coconut pulp
- 50 g heavy cream 33–36%
- 150 g white chocolate 28–30%

- blender/food processor
- thick-bottomed saucepan, silicone spatula

### Method

- grind the peeled fresh coconut pulp into small pieces in a food processor
- place the ground pulp in a saucepan, pour in the cream and place the saucepan on low heat
- warm the mixture up until hot, but do not boil it
- pour the hot mixture over the chocolate, leave for 30–40 seconds, and mix thoroughly with a silicone spatula
- pour the finished ganache into a bowl, cover with cling film touching the surface of the ganache and let it cool slightly
- place in the fridge to stabilize for at least 5–6 hours, preferably overnight

- Mouthwatering ganache with a pleasant crunch of coconut pulp is ready!

You can use it as a filling for a sponge, Napoleon or honey cake, as I did when creating a Chiffon honey cake, which you can see in the carousel

RECIPE FOR CHOCOLATE NAPOLEON CAKE WITH SOUR CHERRIES AND COCONUT

🇺🇦 Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko

A scrumptious ensemble of flavors, embodied in one slice of this cake, will delight your taste buds and boost feel-good hormones!

Dare to check it?

Enjoy the photos, leave a comment and a like as a little something and proceed to the kitchen to put you in a good mood.

#marusya_recipe

### Chocolate shortcrust pastry

- 400 g all-purpose flour
- 40 g alkalized cocoa powder 22–24%
- 2 g salt
- 200 g butter 82%
- 200 g sour cream 20–30%
- 36 g egg yolks (~2 pcs)

### Chocolate Diplomat cream

- 500 g milk 3.2% (1)
- 1 vanilla pod
- 110 g whole eggs (~2 pcs)
- 36 g egg yolks (~2 pcs)
- 200 g caster sugar
- 30 g cornstarch
- 100 g milk 3.2% (2)
- 150 g dark chocolate 54.5%

### Sour cherry sauce

- 500 g pitted sour cherries
- 100 g of caster sugar
- 5g pectin NH Nappage

### Coconut ganache

- 150 g fresh coconut pulp
- 100 g heavy cream 33–36%
- 200 g white chocolate 28–30%

### Shortcrust pastry layers

- Sift the flour with cocoa powder, add salt and mix, then pour onto a work surface. Grate the frozen butter on a coarse grater, dipping it in flour, mix quickly so that the crumbs have formed, and bring them together into a loose pile.
- Run your fingers down the center of the flour-butter crumbs to create a hole, pour in the mixture of cold liquid ingredients and mix gently. Chop the dough with a knife, and quickly shape it into a ball. Divide it into 14 equal parts (~60 g each), shape them into balls and refrigerate for 3–4 hours, preferably overnight.
- Roll out each dough ball on a piece of parchment paper reaching ~12–15 cm in diameter. Roll the rolling pin in flour and roll out the dough layer several times, sprinkling it with the thinnest layer of flour. Cover with a second piece of parchment paper and roll out into a layer ~ 20–22 cm.

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR CHOCOLATE CUPCAKES WITH SALTED CARAMEL
recipes.docx:
🇺🇦 Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko

Chocolate and salted caramel, supremely delicious flavors, merged together in the recipe for these chic, moreish cupcakes.

Get down to baking, these cupcakes won’t disappoint you!

#marusya_recipe

- Cupcake batter ~ 10–12 pcs (50–60 g each)

100 g butter 82%
100 g of dark chocolate 54.5%
165 g of whole eggs (~ 3 pcs)
100 g of caster sugar
1/4 tsp. rock salt
110 g of all-purpose flour
10 g of alkalized cocoa powder (22–24% cocoa butter)
1 tsp. baking powder

### Salted caramel

100 g of caster sugar
10 g of glucose or glucose-fructose syrup
40-50 g of butter 82%
60–75 g of heavy cream 33–36%
1/4 tsp. rock salt

### Dark chocolate ganache

100 g of dark chocolate 54.5%
100 g heavy cream 33–36%

### Chocolate cream cheese frosting

450 g of cream cheese 60–70%
225 g of heavy cream 33–36%
50-100 g of icing sugar (to taste)
15-30 g of alkalized cocoa powder 22–24 % (to taste)

### Batter

- Melt the chocolate and butter over a water bath while stirring. Allow to cool to room temperature.
- Add eggs, sugar and salt to the mixer bowl, whip for around 4–6 minutes until a light and lush mass is formed. With the mixer running, gradually introduce the melted chocolate and butter mixture.
- Sift the flour together with the cocoa powder, add the baking powder and mix. Add the dry ingredients to egg mixture in several lots and fold them in until you get a homogeneous mass.
- Deposit the finished batter into paper cupcakes molds (~50–60 g per mold), filling them by 3/4. Bake in the oven, preheated to 170 °C, for about 20–25 minutes. Check the doneness with a dry skewer.

### Salted caramel

- Pour the sugar into a thick-bottomed saucepan, add glucose or glucose-fructose syrup and place the saucepan over high heat. Meanwhile, bring the cream to a boil in a separate saucepan.

Fans of caramel and chocoholics, get the ingredients ready and treat yourself to an exquisite dessert. Be sure to leave and a comment as a thank you for our humble work

recipes.docx:
🇺🇦Ukrainian version @ma_rusya_manko

Guys, did you know that our chef's generosity knows no bounds?

Discounts for Valentine's Day have just ended, and we are already sharing with you a recipe for a bright, juicy cake which wins the hearts of gourmets over and over again!

Bookmark the recipe, enjoy juicy photos and show the chef your generosity with likes and comments!

#marusya_recipe

### Vanilla sponge

75 g egg yolks (~4 pcs)
70 g caster sugar
10 g vanilla powder
150 g egg whites (~4 pcs)
2 g rock salt
70 g icing sugar
120 g all-purpose flour
20 g cornstarch
3 g baking powder

### Wild berry compote

12 g gelatin 220 Bloom
72 g cold water
100 g raspberry juice
80 g water
30 g caster sugar
130 g wild berries (raspberries, bilberries, blueberries, blackberries, wild strawberries)

### Wild berry mousse

8 g gelatin 220 Bloom
48 g cold water
45 g bilberries
45 g raspberries
65 g heavy cream 33–36% (1)
80 g white chocolate 28-30% (callets)
80 g heavy cream 33–36% (2)
50 g blueberries

### Vanilla cream cheese frosting

500 g cream cheese 60–70%
250 g heavy cream 33–36%
70 g icing sugar
5 g vanilla powder

### Vanilla milk soak

120 g milk 3.2%
100 g caster sugar
5 g vanilla powder

- Buttercream for coating

100 g butter 82.5%
40 g icing sugar
5 g vanilla powder
300 g cream cheese 60–70%

### Sponge

- Beat the egg yolks with 70 g of sugar and 10 g of vanilla powder into a fluffy light mass. Whisk the egg whites together with salt until frothy. Add the icing sugar in several portions and whip the meringue into medium peaks.
- In a large bowl, combine the beaten yolks with the meringue with careful circular movements.
- Combine flour with cornstarch and baking powder, sift through a sieve, add to the egg mass in 2–3 lots and mix carefully until smooth.
- Line an 18-cm cake ring with parchment paper, pour in the batter and put it in the oven, preheated to 180 °C. Bake for ~30–45 minutes until ready.
- Allow the finished sponge to cool, remove it from the mold, wrap in cling film and place in the fridge for 6–8 hours, preferably overnight. Slice into three layers ~2 cm thick.

recipes.title: HOMEMADE HAZELNUT PASTE
recipes.docx:
#marusya_theory_tips

Today I will share with you some tips on how to easily and effortlessly make the hazelnut paste at home.

The first and most important tip for getting an incredibly tasty and fragrant hazelnut paste is to use WELL-TOASTED nuts!

- Got it?
- Brilliant!

To make the hazelnut paste you will need:

- 200 g hazelnuts
- blender/food processor

### Method

- Arrange hazelnuts on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Toast them in the oven preheated to 150 °C for around 20-30 minutes until golden brown, stirring occasionally after the nuts begin to release oil — you should feel a pleasant nutty aroma. Remove skins if necessary.

- I recommend using well-toasted nuts only for making nut paste — for other purposes, such high toasting level is not appropriate, since hazelnuts become slightly bitter.

- Place the well-toasted nuts in the bowl of a blender or food processor and process until they begin to actively release oil and acquire a pasty consistency.

- to get a uniform texture of the paste, use at least 200 g of toasted nuts (depending on the diameter of your blender bowl)
- in the process of grinding, don’t forget to stop the blender and mix the paste with a spatula occasionally, scraping it from the walls of the bowl
- to speed up the blending process, you can add a little odorless vegetable oil, but I usually don’t do this — firstly, the hazelnuts start to release oil during grinding, and secondly, extra oil makes the nut paste runny and, as a result, affects the texture of frosting or ganache made with the addition of nut paste

That's it — the hazelnut paste is ready!

Use the finished nut paste for making various types of fillings and ganaches — it will give them an unforgettable rich nutty flavor!

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR COTTAGE CHEESE STOLLEN
recipes.docx:
Christmas baked goods have a special aroma that can’t be confused with anything else. It can only be described as "magical" — spicy and fruity-nutty notes of these delicacies gather all relatives and friends in one kitchen

Therefore, while the festive season is in full swing, we decided to share with you a recipe for a delicious cottage cheese stollen. And for good reason, it makes two stollens ~ 1 kg each — absolutely everyone who had a chance to try it was delighted! And one should have been quick, since my 1 kg stollen disappeared in half a day!

So, here’s the stollen recipe:

#marusya_recipe

### Spiced Dried Fruits

- 150 g golden raisins
- 100 g dried apricots
- 150 g dried cranberries
- ~100–120 g of spiced or dark rum

### Roasted Nut Halves

- 140 g almonds
- 60 g hazelnuts

### Dough

- 250 g butter 82% (1)
- 200 g of caster sugar
- 130 g whole eggs
- 200 g cottage cheese 9%
- 10 g vanilla powder
- zest of one orange
- zest of one lemon
- ~60–70 g lemon juice
- 400 g all-purpose flour (1)
- 20 g baking powder
- 100 g all-purpose flour (2)
- ~500 g spiced dried fruits
- 200 g roasted nuts halves
- 80 g butter 82% (2)

### Spiced dried fruits

Wash dried fruits thoroughly and dry them with a paper towel. Cut dried apricots into small pieces.
- Pour rum over the dried fruits, mix, cover with cling film on top and leave at room temperature overnight.

### Roasted nut halves

- Place raw hazelnuts and almonds on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Toast in the oven, preheated to 150 °C, for about 10-15 minutes until lightly browned and aromatic.
- Remove from the oven and allow to cool completely. Skin the nuts and cut them into halves.

### Dough

- Place soft butter (1) and sugar in a mixer bowl and beat first at medium and then at high speed until doubled in volume. Add room temperature eggs one at a time, mixing thoroughly after each addition.

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR THE UPSIDE-DOWN BANANA PIE
recipes.docx:
A simple pie with a stunning appearance!

This amazing delicacy is a must-try for all fans of banana desserts! But even if you are not one of them, I still suggest baking this upside-down pie for three reasons:

- the pie is very nutritious and its vegan
- the preparation time is just 15 min!
- your kitchen will be filled with the most mouthwatering aroma!

P.S. Be quick to taste it as it disappears in 15 min as well

This is a charity recipe, and in the profile header l/stories you can find a link for donations. Follow it to help people affected by war in Ukraine.

- 100% OF THE FUNDS RAISED will go to humanitarian aid to Ukrainians

YOU CAN DONATE FOLLOWING THE LINK IN THE PROFILE HEADER AND STORIES

🇺🇦 Together we stay strong!

#marusya_recipe

### Dry caramel-coated bananas

- 4-5 bananas
- 100 g caster sugar
- 1 tsp. glucose or glucose-fructose syrup

### Batter

- 50 g odorless vegetable oil
- 150 g water
- 100 g all-purpose flour
- 15 g cornstarch
- 10 g baking powder
- 50 g semolina
- 50 g caster sugar
- 1 g salt
- 20 g desiccated coconut
- zest of one orange

### Dry caramel-coated bananas

- Pour sugar into a thick-bottomed saucepan, add glucose or glucose-fructose syrup, and place over high heat.

- Shaking the saucepan occasionally, wait until the sugar has completely melted and a dry light amber caramel has formed.

- Meanwhile, peel the bananas and cut them in half lengthwise.

- As soon as the caramel acquires a light amber color, pour it into a cake pan. Scrape the bottom and sides of the saucepan with a silicone spatula, carefully collecting remainder caramel.

- I bake in a silicone mold d = 24 cm
It is better to fill the saucepan with water immediately, as dry caramel hardens very quickly

- Arrange peeled bananas one next to each other on the bottom of the pan on top of hot dry caramel in one layer.

### Batter

- Sift flour, mix it with a whisk with baking powder, starch and salt. Add semolina, sugar, desiccated coconut and orange zest, mix again. Pour the mixture into a mixer bowl.

recipes.title: HOW TO MAKE VANILLA POWDER AT HOME
recipes.docx:
#marusya_theory_tips

Today I will share with you a little secret on how to easily and effortlessly make natural vanilla powder at home.

It is made from scraped vanilla pods — usually we remove the seeds and use them to make a variety of fillings and frosting. But experienced confectioners know that empty pods can also be reused. For example, to make vanilla powder.

So, to make the vanilla powder you will need:

◽3 g scraped vanilla pods
◽30 g caster sugar

- coffee grinder

### Preparation

▫ Cut the vanilla pods in half lengthwise, remove the seeds (use them to make any dessert of your choice)
▫ dry the pods in the oven until brittle
- if the scraped pods have been stored for a long time and become dry, you can skip this step
▫cut the pods with scissors into medium pieces to fit in your coffee grinder
▫ add sugar
▫ grind everything into powder

That's it — the vanilla powder is ready!

You can use it to add an incredibly spiced aroma to your pastries!

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR THE BASQUE BURNT CHEESECAKE SAN SEBASTIAN
recipes.docx:
Guys, today my team and I would like to share with you a recipe for a super-popular cheesecake that delighted LITERALLY EVERYONE who tried it.

I baked this cheesecake about a dozen times, experimenting with the ingredients, their proportions and baking modes, before I achieved the perfectly balanced taste and desired texture.

The silky texture of the cheesecake, similar to the delicious soft serve vanilla ice cream, and the baked caramelized crust on the outside, accompanied with a cup of coffee in the morning, are guaranteed to put you in a great mood for the whole day.

In the profile header you can find a link for donations. Follow it to help people affected by the war in Ukraine.

- 100% OF THE FUNDS RAISED will go to humanitarian aid to Ukrainians

YOU CAN DONATE FOLLOWING THE LINK IN THE PROFILE HEADER

🇺🇦Together we stay strong!

#marusya_recipe

### Ingredients

- 270 g cream cheese 60-70%
- 250 g mascarpone 80-85%
- 460 g heavy cream 33-36%
- 140 g of caster sugar
- 240 g whole eggs (~4.4 pcs)
- 30 g all-purpose flour
- 30–50 g vanilla paste

### Preparation process

- Line a cake ring or spring form pan (d = 18 cm, h = 8-10 cm) with two sheets of parchment paper.
- Place all the ingredients in a blender bowl and process until smooth.
- Pour the mixture into the cake ring. Bake the cheesecake for about 30 minutes at 230 °C until its top is burnt. The finished cheesecake should have the edges set and the middle still wobbly.
- Allow the cheesecake to cool down slightly at room temperature, and then place it in the fridge to stabilize.
- Take the cheesecake out of the fridge, remove the ring and parchment paper.

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR THE HONEY CAKE WITH SEA BUCKTHORN CURD
recipes.docx:
You can find a link to download the PDF-recipe for donation to help people affected by the war in the profile header.

- 100% OF THE FUNDS RAISED will go to humanitarian aid to Ukrainians

YOU CAN DONATE FOLLOWING THE LINK IN THE PROFILE HEADER

🇺🇦Together we stay strong!

#marusya_recipe

### Honey Dough
- 210 g of caster sugar
- 90 g honey
- 165 g whole eggs (~3 pcs)
- 160 g butter 82%
- 10 g of baking soda
- 1 tsp. lemon juice or 1/3 tsp. citric acid 600 g all-purpose flour

### Sea Buckthorn Curd
- 200 g sea buckthorn (fresh or frozen)
- 80 g of caster sugar
- 60 g butter 82%
- 2-3 egg yolks

### Sour Cream Frosting
- 800 g of drained sour cream 30%
- 100 g of icing sugar
- 1 vanilla pod or 25 g vanilla paste

- Sour Cream Frosting for Coating
- 400 g of drained sour cream 30%
- 60 g of icing sugar
- 1 vanilla pod or 15 g vanilla paste

### Honey dough

- Place sugar, honey, eggs and butter in a thick-bottomed saucepan, put it over low heat and, stirring constantly, wait until the butter and honey have completely dissolved. Remove from the heat, add lemon juice or citric acid, baking soda, and mix thoroughly. The mixture should foam well and increase in volume.

- Incorporate the sifted flour in several additions and mix a soft dough with a tablespoon, let it sit for 15-20 minutes.

- Divide the dough into 4 equal pieces, roll each of them on a piece of parchment paper into a thin rectangular layer ~ 32 x 22 cm, cutting off the excess dough each time. Collect the scraps, shape them and roll out a 5th cake layer of the same size. Prick the layers with a fork and bake in the oven for about 5-6 minutes at 170-180 °C.

- Using a ruler and a knife, cut rectangles measuring 30 x 20 cm out of still hot layers, then cut them in half into strips ~ 15 x 20 cm.

### Sea Buckthorn Curd

- Place sea buckthorn in a thick-bottomed saucepan, add 3-4 tbsp. water and bring to a boil. Cool slightly, process with a blender and pass through a sieve.

recipes.title: RECIPE FOR BANANA CUPCAKES WITH RUM
recipes.docx:
Guys, today I’ve prepared for you a recipe for incredibly delicious banana–vanilla cupcakes made from almond flour. These moist cupcakes are complemented by airy domes of caramel frosting and are generously topped with banana caramel, flavored with spiced dark rum.

This is a charity recipe, so today in the profile header you can find a link for donations. Follow it to help people affected by the war in Ukraine.

- 100% OF THE FUNDS RAISED will go to humanitarian aid to Ukrainians

When I see a notification that someone has donated some sum, this makes me even more confident that there are many people among you who are ready to help others in difficult times! Thank you so much for everyone

🇺🇦 Together we stay strong!

YOU CAN DONATE USING THE BANK DETAILS IN THE PROFILE HEADER

#marusya_recipe

- Batter ~18–20 pcs. 45–50 g each

100 g butter 82%
100 g caster sugar
120 g whole eggs (~2 pcs)
1 tsp. vanilla paste or extract
150 g all–purpose flour
10 g baking powder
100 g almond flour
1–2 g rock salt
1/2 tsp. cinnamon
3/4 tsp. baking soda
225 g ripe bananas (~2–3 pcs)
100 g sour cream 20–25%
2 tbsp. dark rum

### Banana Caramel

125 g caster sugar
50 g glucose syrup
150 g heavy cream 33–36%
70 g banana puree
1 tsp. vanilla paste
15 g dark rum
60 g butter 82%
1/3–1/4 tsp. rock salt

### Banana Caramel–Rum Frosting

660 g mascarpone 80–85%
340 g banana caramel
30 g dark rum

### Batter

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl, add sugar and beat for about 3 min using a paddle attachment with a silicone edge until a light, fluffy mass has formed.
- Introduce the eggs one at a time, each time thoroughly mixing the mass until smooth. Add vanilla paste, combine.
- Sift flour together with baking powder, cinnamon and baking soda. Add almond flour, salt and mix with a whisk.
- Process 225 g of ripe bananas into a puree, add sour cream and rum, combine.
- Add half of the banana–sour cream mixture to the mixer bowl, mix. Reduce the mixer speed, add dry ingredients, and mix. Add the second part of the liquid ingredients, mix again.

recipes.title: CHARITY RECIPE FOR LEMON-POPPY SEED CUPCAKE
recipes.docx:
Guys, today we’d like to share a recipe for amazingly delicious cupcakes! Domes of silky frosting made with white chocolate and Limoncello liqueur perfectly harmonize with airy poppy seed cupcakes and lemon curd filling. I’m sure you’ll definitely enjoy their rich taste with prominent sourness and delicate texture with pleasantly crunchy poppy seeds!

As promised, today, on the day the recipe is posted, there’s a link for donations placed in the profile header. Follow it to help people affected by the war in Ukraine.

- 100% OF THE FUNDS RAISED will go to humanitarian aid to Ukrainians

Bookmark the recipe, make cupcakes for your loved ones and don't forget to support Ukrainians who don't have such an opportunity now. Any of your contributions matters — I’m sure, even $5 will make a difference and we will be able to help Ukrainian families!

YOU CAN DONATE USING THE BANK DETAILS IN THE PROFILE HEADER

#marusya_recipe

- Batter ~12 pcs, 50-60 g each

180 g whole eggs (~3 pcs)
175 g caster sugar
120 g heavy cream 33-36%
75 g butter 82%
10 g poppy seeds
zest of 3 lemons
170 g all-purpose flour
1.5 tsp. baking powder
1/4 tsp. salt

### Lemon Curd

65 g lemon juice
35 g caster sugar
50 g egg yolks (~2.5 pcs)
35 g butter 82%
zest of one lemon

### Frosting

90 g heavy cream 33-36% (1)
zest of one lemon
120 g white chocolate 30%
120 g heavy cream 33-36% (2)
20 g Limoncello liqueur or lemon juice
180 g mascarpone 80-85%
2-3 pinches of ground saffron or 2-3 drops of yellow coloring

### Batter

- Place eggs and sugar in the mixer bowl and whip on medium-maximum speed for about 2 min using a whisk attachment until a light foam has appeared. Pour in the cream and whip for about 2 min more until smooth.
- Place butter in a thick-bottomed saucepan and melt it, add poppy seeds with lemon zest, mix until smooth.
- Sift flour, mix it with baking powder and salt. Reduce the mixer speed, add dry ingredients and mix until smooth. Add the warm butter, poppy seed and lemon zest mixture, mix thoroughly.

recipes.title: HAZELNUT-CHOCOLATE CUPCAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
#marusya_recipe

### Crumble

100 g hazelnuts
80 g caster sugar
3 g cinnamon powder
1/4 tsp. salt

- Batter ~28-30 pcs.

250 g sour cream 20-30%
130 g Greek yogurt 10-12%
1.5 tsp. baking soda
180 g whole eggs (~3 pcs)
200 g caster sugar
250 g butter 82%
1 tbsp. rum
2 tsp. vanilla paste
460 g all-purpose flour
2 tsp. baking powder
1 tsp. salt

### Ganache

240 g milk chocolate 33%
80 g hazelnut paste
200 g heavy cream 33-36% (1)
250 g heavy cream 33-36% (2)
300 g mascarpone 80-85%

### Crumble

- Roast the hazelnuts in the oven until golden brown and a pronounced nutty flavor, then cool down completely.

- if you’re using unskinned hazelnuts, skin them after roasting

- Put the roasted hazelnuts, sugar, cinnamon powder and salt into the bowl of a blender / food processor. Grind in pulses into fine crumbs.

### Batter

- Combine sour cream and yogurt with baking soda and set the mixture aside for 10-15 min. Place the eggs and sugar in a blender bowl and beat for a minute. Add soft butter, and beat again until smooth.

- Add rum and vanilla paste to the sour cream and yogurt mixture, mix. Pour the mixture into a blender bowl and carefully process in pulses until smooth. Transfer the mixture in a large bowl.

- Sift the flour, mix it with baking powder and salt, add to liquid ingredients and mix thoroughly with a silicone spatula.

- Transfer the batter to a piping bag and pipe it into paper molds, filling them 1/3 full. Sprinkle ~1 tsp. of crumble on top of each cupcake. Pipe the second layer of batter on top, filling the paper molds 3/4 full. Sprinkle the cupcakes with the remaining hazelnut crumble, pressing it lightly with a teaspoon into the batter.

- Bake in the oven, preheated to 180-200 °C, for about 15 min. Check the doneness with a dry skewer. Remove from the oven, allow to cool down completely.

recipes.title: RASPBERRY-LEMON CUPCAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
I know that you enjoy baking using the recipes from my profile. Today I’ve got a new recipe for you to take advantage of the fresh raspberries available on the supermarkets' shelves. Please, welcome stunningly beautiful Raspberry-Lemon cupcakes, full of rich, balanced flavors!

Light lemon notes of pleasantly sour frosting perfectly complement fragrant and incredibly tasty cupcakes, made with the addition of raspberries and lemon zest.

By the way, the team and I want to post free recipes in the profile 2 times more often. How do you like the idea? If you support it, let me know in the comments and don't forget to thank us with your - it takes you a few seconds, but means a lot to us

So here's the cupcake recipe!

#marusya_recipe

- Batter ~ 12-14 pcs. ~60 g each

125 g butter 82%
zest of two lemons
200 g caster sugar
180 g whole eggs (~3 pcs)
120 g sour cream 20-30%
160 g all-purpose flour
1.5 tsp. baking powder
1/4 tsp. salt
150 g fresh raspberries

### Lemon Curd

60 g whole eggs (~1 pc.)
36 g egg yolks (~2 pcs)
90 g lemon juice
90 g caster sugar
75 g butter 82%

### Frosting

270 g lemon curd
330 g mascarpone 80-85%

### Batter

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl, add lemon zest and sugar, and beat at medium or maximum speed for about 3 min using a paddle attachment with a rubber edge until a light, fluffy mass is formed. Add eggs one at a time and mix until smooth. Add sour cream, combine.
- Sift flour, mix it with baking powder and salt. Reduce the mixer speed, add dry ingredients and mix until smooth. Add fresh raspberries and gently incorporate them at low speed for 10 sec.
- Add ~ 60 g of the finished batter into each paper cupcake cup, filling it by ~ 3/4.
- Bake in the oven, preheated to 190 °C, for about 20-25 min. Check the doneness with a dry skewer. Remove the cupcakes from the oven and let them cool down completely.

- if you bake with a "fan" mode on, reduce the temperature to 170 °C

recipes.title: APRICOT-AMARETTO CHEESECAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
#marusya_recipe

Summer, like the season of apricots, has come to an end, but the team and I can’t miss the opportunity to share with you a recipe for the delicate Apricot-Amaretto cheesecake.

If apricots are not available, I advise you to replace them with sweet peaches or nectarines and treat yourself to an easy-to-prepare, but very tasty dessert.

Don’t forget that your like before bookmarking the recipe is the best gratitude for our humble work!

🇺🇦 I also want to remind you that only a few hours left until the end of the SALE “50% OFF ON ALL PRODUCTS”Check out all the details in stories.

So, let’s get back to the recipe. To prepare this cheesecake, you'll need a cake ring (d = 22-24 cm, h = 6 cm).

### Crust

200 g shortcrust crumble or biscuits
80 g almond flakes
10 g desiccated coconut
40-50 g butter 82%

### Cream cheese layer

850 g cream cheese 60-70%
160 g caster sugar
280 g whole eggs (~5 pcs)
85 g sour cream 20-30%
70 g of Amaretto liquor
1 tsp. vanilla paste
zest of one orange

### Decoration

400 g fresh apricots
1 tbsp. caster sugar
1 tbsp. rum
1 tbsp. Amaretto liquor
15-20 g almond flakes

### Crust

- Lightly roast almond flakes in the oven at 160-170 °C for about 5-6 min until golden brown, cool and crush them with your hands.
Grind the crumble in a food processor until fine crumbs have formed.
- Mix ground crumbs with crushed almond flakes and desiccated coconut. Add soft butter and mix until smooth.
- Wrap the bottom of the cake ring tightly with foil. Form the cheesecake crust by pressing the mixture firmly into the bottom. Place it in the freezer for at least 30 min.

### Cream cheese layer

- Mix the cream cheese with sugar at low speed until creamy, then gradually add the eggs and mix thoroughly until smooth. Add sour cream, pour in the Amaretto liquor and mix again. Then add vanilla paste, orange zest, and mix.
- Take the ring with the crust out of the freezer and pour in the cream cheese mixture. Bake the cheesecake for about 100-120 min at 120-130 °C with a water bath.

recipes.title: STRAWBERRY-WHITE CHOCOLATE-VANILLA CUPCAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
RU @ma_rusya_manko

#marusya_recipe

The strawberry season comes to its end, as if telling us that half of the hot summer has passed. To make the most out of it, I’ve got a recipe for moist, tender and breathtakingly delicious cupcakes.

I strongly advise you to make these cupcakes, even if the strawberry is no longer available. In this case, just replace it with any other berry - I'm sure the cupcakes will still turn out brilliantly!

- Batter ~20-22 pcs

250 g butter 82%
200 g caster sugar
1 tsp. vanilla paste
240 g whole eggs (~ 4 pcs)
120 g all-purpose flour
10 g baking powder
1/4 tsp. salt
140 g almond flour
200 g strawberries

### Strawberry marmalade

300 g strawberry puree
30 g caster sugar
3 g pectin NH Nappage
15 g lemon juice

### Frosting

70 g heavy cream 33-36 % (1)
70 g white chocolate
120 g heavy cream 33-36 % (2)
1 tbsp. vanilla paste
250 g mascarpone
100 g strawberry marmalade

### Batter

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl, add sugar and vanilla paste, and beat with a paddle attachment until a light fluffy mass is formed.

- Add room temperature eggs one at a time, mix until smooth.

- After adding the eggs, the butter mixture may split - at this stage it’s OK

- Sift the flour, mix with baking powder, salt and almond flour. Reduce the mixer speed to minimum, and incorporate dry ingredients in 2-3 portions.

- Almond flour can be substituted for ground almonds, processed in pulses.

- Wash strawberries, dry with a paper towel, carefully remove the calyx and cut into small cubes.

- Add strawberry cubes to the mixer bowl and carefully combine everything with a silicone spatula.

- Fill paper cupcake liners with the batter (~ 50-55 g each), filling them by ~ 3/4.

- Bake in the oven, preheated to 200 °C, for about 20 minutes. Check the doneness with a skewer.

### Strawberry marmalade

recipes.title: BANANA TEA CAKE WITH DATES AND NUTS
recipes.docx:
Catch the recipe for an amazingly delicious, yet easy-to-make tea cake. If you serve it with buttercream and caramel-banana sauce — you’ll definitely be paid high compliments!

The recipe for caramel sauce makes quite a large portion, but it’s just perfect for waffles, crepes, pancakes, or just to accompany your coffee or tea.

Those who are wild about banana and caramel flavors, please, welcome!

#marusya_recipe

### Tea Cake

260 g chopped dates
200 g brown sugar
80 g butter 82%
60 g dark rum
180 g water
1/2 tsp. baking soda
80 g whole eggs
130 g bananas
1 tsp. vanilla paste
100 g walnuts
1 tsp. salt
260 g all-purpose flour
10 g baking powder

### Caramel-Banana Sauce

125 g caster sugar
50 g glucose syrup
150 g heavy cream 33-36%
70 g banana puree
1 tsp. vanilla paste
15 g dark rum
60 g butter 82%
1/3 tsp. salt

- Buttercream for decoration:

265 g cream cheese
135 g heavy cream 33-36%
30 g icing sugar
3 g vanilla paste

2 rectangular molds ~22x9 cm, h=10 cm

### Tea cakes

- Lightly roast the walnuts in the oven at 170-180 °C for about 5-6 minutes until light golden color and pleasant aroma. Let them cool down and coarse chop them.

- Put sugar, butter, water, rum and chopped dates in a saucepan. Stirring occasionally, heat the mixture until sugar and butter have dissolved. Then increase the heat and bring the mixture to a boil. Remove the saucepan from the heat, pour the mixture into a large bowl and let it cool down to room temperature.

- if you do not want to use alcohol, you can replace it with water

- In a separate bowl, beat eggs, banana puree and vanilla paste until fluffy. Pour into the cooled mixture, add baking soda and mix until smooth. Add chopped walnuts, and mix again.

- Combine flour, baking powder and salt, sift. Add to the batter and mix until smooth.

- Grease the molds with butter and dust them with some flour. Pour the batter into the molds, filling them approximately ⅔ (~ 680 g of batter per 1 tea cake).

See the continuation of the recipe in the photo carousel ⏩

recipes.title: CARAMEL AND STRAWBERRY HONEY CAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

#marusya_recipe

I’d like to share this recipe although it is not new, as the first juicy and fragrant strawberries have become available on the market.

The cake is definitely worth your attention, so I suggest not to put it off for a long time and treat yourself and your family during the berry season.

Before you save the recipe, don't forget to support me and my team with your likes

### Cake Layers

500 g all-purpose flour
200 g caster sugar
140 g butter 82%
115 g whole eggs
80 g honey
6 g baking soda
3 g citric acid

### Strawberry Confit

250 g strawberry puree
1 tbsp. lemon/lime juice
30 g caster sugar
3 g pectin NH Nappage

### Caramel Frosting

100 g butter 82%
370 g caramel condensed milk
70 g drained sour cream 25-30%

### Cream Cheese Frosting

400 g cream cheese 60-65%
120 g heavy cream 33-36%
20 g icing sugar
1 tsp. vanilla paste

### Cake Layers

- Melt the sugar in a thick-bottomed saucepan (do not stir it). While sugar is melting, heat up honey and butter.

- Remove the saucepan from the heat and pour hot honey into the melted sugar, mix. Then add the melted hot butter and mix well again. Let the mixture cool down to ~70 °C.

- Incorporate a third of the flour and all the eggs into the caramel mixture, mix until smooth and add baking soda and citric acid. Mix vigorously until the mixture has foamed well. Add the rest of the flour and mix with a tablespoon until well incorporated. Let the dough cool down for about 15 minutes.

- Divide the dough into 5 equal pieces. Roll out each piece on parchment paper into a thin layer 2-3 mm thick, then cut out an even rectangle ~24x34 cm. Roll out a thin layer from the scraps of dough, which will later be needed for making crumbs.

- Prick the layers with a fork and bake in a preheated oven at 170 °C for 4-6 minutes until golden brown. While the cake layers are still hot, trim off the edges to get rectangles measuring 20x30 cm.

recipes.title: MANGO AND PASSION FRUIT INDIVIDUAL CHEESECAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

#marusya_recipe

A crispy shortcrust base with almond flakes, an exotic taste of refreshing passion fruit sourness in a delicate cream cheese layer with pieces of sweet mango sprinkled with vanilla seeds - you can taste all these splendid textures by preparing these fantastically bright individual Mango and Passion Fruit Cheesecakes.

I remind you that a like before bookmarking the recipe is the best gratitude for our humble work!

I also would like to remind you that today is Wednesday, which means we start a new charity sale of the week with an unprecedented discount of -85% for a set of 6 recipes with educational videos! Check out all details in stories

So let's get back to the recipe. To prepare these individual cheesecakes, I used 9 rings d=9 cm, h=5.5 cm (see the picture in carousel)

### Cheesecake base
60 g almond flakes
240 g shortcrust crumble or biscuits
0.5 tsp ground cinnamon
0.5 tsp ground star anise
50 g butter 82%

### Cream cheese layer
150 g passion fruit puree without seeds
10 g cornstarch
750 g cream cheese
200 g granulated sugar
80 g sour cream 20-30%
165 g whole eggs
54 g egg yolks

### Topping
180 g mango puree
200 g fresh or frozen diced mango (1x1 cm cubes)
3 g pectin NH Nappage
45 g granulated sugar
1 vanilla pod

### Cheesecake base
- Lightly roast almond flakes in the oven at 160-170°C for about 5-6 minutes until light golden brown, let them cool down and crush with your hands.
- Grind the crumble in a food processor until fine crumbs form.
- Mix the crumble with crushed almond flakes and spices. Add softened butter and mix until smooth.
- Wrap the bottom of the rings tightly with foil. Form the cheesecake bases by pressing the mixture to the bottom of the rings. Place them in the freezer for at least 30 minutes.

- use ready-made shortbread cookies or self-made crumble (the recipe and the video of baking and forming the cheesecake base is available as a bonus to the set of 6 recipes which is at the sale of the week)

recipes.title: EASTER CAKE RECIPE — KULICH WITH EGG YOLKS
recipes.docx:
This recipe for Easter cake is not new, but it is 100% foolproof. For the last 6 years I have baked double or even triple batches of Easter cakes using it.

I used to sell some of the cakes to my neighbors and acquaintances, and those kuliches that remained, disappeared in 3-4 days, as a rule. Even this year, despite the lack of conditions, I will make at least one batch.

This Easter cakes are incredibly tasty, moderately moist and airy. They do not crumble and remain soft for a long time.

- Before proceeding to the recipe, I also want to remind you that the Easter sale -50% for all recipes and online courses started yesterday. You can check out the full range of recipes available for purchase in stories or in the highlights

So, for the preferment you need:

- 200 ml of warm milk
- 1 tbsp. of sugar
- 15 g of dry yeast / 45 g of fresh yeast
- 150 g of flour

For the dough:

- preferment
- 300 ml of warm milk
- 120 g of egg yolks (7-8 pcs)
- 200 g of sugar
- 50 g of trimoline
- 2 vanilla pods
- 0.5 tsp of salt
- 750 g of flour
- 125 g of butter
- raisins, candied fruits, dried fruits, orange zest and lemon zest soaked in rum - to taste (I have ~ 300 g)

- Wash the dried fruits, let them dry, cut into pieces if necessary, add the candied fruits, then add rum, cognac or orange juice and leave at least overnight. Drain off excess liquid before use.

Making the preferment:

- Pour warm milk into a large bowl, add sugar and stir. Mix dry yeast with flour, sift through a sieve and add to warm milk. Mix thoroughly and leave for 0.5-1.5 hours until the dough increases in volume by 2.5-3 times.

- If you use fresh yeast, add it to the milk with sugar, leave for 5-10 minutes and mix thoroughly. Then add sifted flour, mix well until homogeneous and leave in a warm place.

CUPCAKE WITH GUINNESS BEER AND BAILEYS LIQUEUR RECIPE by @marusya.manko

#marusya_recipe

There should have been a few paragraphs of introduction from me, but there won't be. I just can't say anything right now. I feel like I’m in some dark place and don't know how to get out of it yet. When it gets easier, I'll let you know.

You can say “thank you” to the team, as this post appears thanks to them - I'm just not able to do anything at all right now.

for 12 cupcakes*
* I advise you to immediately prepare a double portion

### Batter

120 g Guinness beer
120 g butter 82%
30 g alkalized cocoa powder
180 g granulated sugar
65 g sour cream 20-30%
60 g whole eggs (1 large egg)
1 tsp vanilla paste
130 g all-purpose flour
1/4 tsp salt
1 tsp baking soda

- Frosting with Baileys

125 g mascarpone
45 g Baileys liqueur
20 g icing sugar

### Soaking

120 g Baileys liqueur

### Chocolate ganache

100 g dark chocolate 54.5%
100 g heavy cream 33-36%

### Batter

- Put butter and beer in a saucepan and put it over medium heat. Stirring occasionally, wait until the butter has completely melted, without bringing the mixture to a boil.
- As soon as the butter has melted, add cocoa powder mixed with sugar. Mix thoroughly and remove the saucepan from the heat.
- Beat sour cream, eggs and vanilla paste until smooth. Add to the mixture in the saucepan and mix thoroughly.
- Sift flour, add salt and baking soda, mix thoroughly. Pour the mixture of dry ingredients into the liquid, mix until smooth.
- Pour the batter into cupcake molds, filling them ~2/3 full. Bake for about 20 minutes at 195°C. Check the doneness of the cupcakes with a wooden skewer.

- 195 °C with "top-bottom" / "bottom" mode
175 °C with "fan" mode

- Frosting with Baileys

- Place well-chilled mascarpone cheese in the mixer bowl, add icing sugar and Baileys liqueur. Beat with a whisk attachment until a creamy consistency is obtained.
- Make holes in the center of completely cooled cupcakes using the back of any pastry tip and gently pushing it into each cupcake.

recipes.docx:
#marusya_recipe

Guys, I really need your support right now ‼ A and a few words of gratitude in the comments will be more than enough!

Please, show me all the love you can give

It turned out that continuing to work now is much more difficult than I thought. It seems that you have lifted a heavy slab and are trying to carry it. A slab that can collapse at any moment and crush you down with its weight.

In such a psychological state, it is especially difficult to experience betrayal. And I was betrayed twice yesterday.

I thank God for my family, for my team, and also for all of you! For the fact that I have you, that I can always count on your support, love and understanding!

Bookmark the recipe. I hope that very soon every Ukrainian will be able to cook in quiet and peace in their own kitchen, amen 🇺🇦

Cake ring d = 22-24 cm, h = 6-8 cm

### Base

40 g walnuts
200 g shortbread crumble or biscuits
25 g Dutch-processed (alkalized) cocoa powder
25 g brown sugar
40 g butter 82%
3 big bananas

### Cream Cheese Layer

375 g white chocolate
375 g cream cheese
180 g whole eggs (~3 pcs.)
220 g sour cream 20-30% or heavy cream 33%
1 tbsp vanilla paste or vanilla extract

- Dark Chocolate Ganache with Banana

125 g dark chocolate 70%
75 g heavy cream 33-36%
100 g banana puree

### Milk Chocolate Ganache

150 g milk chocolate
100 g heavy cream 33-36%

### Base

- Lightly roast the nuts in the oven at 180 °C for about 5-6 minutes, cool them down and chop into small pieces. Grind the biscuits in a food processor into fine crumbs.
- Mix the crumbs with cocoa powder, sugar and nuts. Melt the butter and pour it into the dry ingredients. Stir thoroughly.
- Wrap the bottom of the ring tightly with some foil. Form the base of the cheesecake in a ring, firmly pressing the crumbs to the bottom, make the layer even and tamp it with a spoon. Place it in the freezer for at least 30 minutes.

- Check out a link to a live broadcast in stories, where I describe in detail how to cook a delicious shortbread crumble for a cheesecake

recipes.title: BLUEBERRY, LEMON AND ALMOND TEACAKES RECIPE by @marusya.manko
recipes.docx:
Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

#ma_rusya_recipe

Check out the recipe for amazingly tender, moist and incredibly delicious cupcakes with lemon zest and juice, blueberries and almond flour.

Guys, I share from the bottom of my heart, having invested a lot of effort in the creation of this recipe, so I expect the same return from you! Bookmark the recipe and leave me a little heart as “thank you”

- This is super important to me

If I see that you value my time and warmly support the desire to share free recipes, I will definitely give away them more often

- 200 g soft butter 82%
- 150 g of sugar
lemon zest of 1 lemon
- 250 g eggs (~5 pcs)
- 200 g almond flour
- 50 g all-purpose flour
- 1/4 tsp baking powder
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 60 g lemon juice
- 100-120 g fresh or frozen blueberries

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl along with sugar and lemon zest, beat with a paddle attachment until a light and fluffy mass is formed.

- Add the room temperature eggs (one at a time), mix until smooth and add the almond flour.

- you can substitute almond flour with almonds processed in pulses into small pieces

- Sift the all-purpose flour, mix it with baking powder and salt, and add to the mixer bowl. Reduce the speed to minimum. Pour in the lemon juice.

- Fill the paper cups with the finished batter, using ~ 45-50 g per cupcake (the recipe makes 18-20 pcs). Add a few blueberries on top, lightly dipping them into the batter.

- Bake in the oven, preheated to 180°C (160°C if the fan is on), for about 25-30 minutes, check the readiness with a skewer.

- 200 g cream cheese
- 100 g heavy cream 33-36%
- 20 g icing sugar
- 1 tsp violet paste from Sosa
- 80 g fresh blueberries

- Put the well-chilled cream cheese and cream in a mixer bowl, add icing sugar and violet paste. Beat with a whisk attachment until a stable and smooth creamy mass is formed.

- Using a Closed Star tip pipe a dome on top of each cupcake and decorate it with a blueberry.

recipes.title: EGG YOLK AND BUTTER TEA CAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
by @marusya.manko

Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

#ma_rusya_recipe

I’ve got an interesting story of the creation of this recipe. Six months ago I visited my sister in Germany and made an appointment with an endocrinologist.

Since the doctor turned out to be a family friend of my German acquaintances, whom I once treated with a Kyiv cake, he, instead of paying, asked me to bake this particular cake for him.

After making the cake, there were a lot of yolks, butter and some sweet condensed milk left. Apart from that, I used everything I could find in the fridge.

The tea cake came out so tender and tasty that my sister's husband fell in love with it and after my departure repeatedly asked her to bake it.

200 g butter
120 g sugar
100 g sweet condensed milk
160 g egg yolks (~9 pcs.)
55 g whole eggs (~1 pc.)
60 g heavy cream 30-33%
50 g Baileys liqueur
300 g all-purpose flour
10 g baking powder
5 g salt (~1 level tsp)
100 g nuts
100 g raisins

2 rectangular molds ~22x10 cm

- Place soft butter in a mixer bowl, add sugar and beat until fluffy.
- if you are using Kenwood, choose a flat beater attachment with silicone edges

- Add sweet condensed milk to the mixture, and beat again until fluffy.

- Add the yolks one at a time, then add the whole egg and mix until smooth.
- if yolks are not available, just use 4 whole eggs

- Reduce the mixer speed to minimum and add cream and liqueur. Mix until smooth.
- if you don’t have liqueur or cream available, replace them with 100 g milk

- Mix flour with baking powder and salt. Then add to the mixture and mix until smooth.

Add sweet condensed milk to the mixture, and beat again until fluffy.
Add the yolks one at a time, then add the whole egg and mix until smooth.
if yolks are not available, just use 4 whole eggs
Reduce the mixer speed to minimum and add cream and liqueur. Mix until smooth.
if you don’t have liqueur or cream available, replace them with 100 g milk
Mix flour with baking powder and salt. Then add to the mixture and mix until smooth.

recipes.title: RAFFAELLO’ ZEPHYR RECIPE
recipes.docx:
by @marusya.manko

Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

#ma_rusya_recipe

### Apple jam

- 500 g baked Granny Smith apples
- 2-3 tbsp. water
- 150 g sugar
- 7 g pectin

- Place the baked apples into a saucepan, add a couple of tbsp. of water, 100 g of sugar and put it over low heat. When the sugar has completely dissolved, switch the heat to medium and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally. Let it simmer for about 2-3 minutes.
- Process the hot mixture with a blender until completely homogeneous and pass it through a sieve if desired.
- Place the puree over low heat and, stirring constantly, gradually sprinkle in 50 g of sugar mixed with 7 g of pectin. Bring the mixture to a boil and keep it boiling constantly mixing for about 7-8 minutes.
- Cool the puree down to 30-35 °C.

- ‘Raffaello’ zephyr

- ~450-500 g apple jam
- 7-8 g albumin
- 100 g water
- 30-40 g coconut water
- 50 g of Malibu rum
- 10-12 g agar-agar 1200 bloom
- 250 g sugar
- 150 g glucose or glucose and fructose syrup
- 120 g white chocolate
- 40 g dessicated coconut
- 40 g roasted blanched almonds

- Pour the jam into a mixer bowl, add 7-8 g of albumin, mix thoroughly and set it aside for 15 minutes, then put whipping at slow speed.
- instead of albumin, you can use 45-50 g of raw egg white. In the latter case, I advise you to cook the jam longer and let it stabilize overnight in the refrigerator.

- Pour 100 g of water, 50 g of rum and coconut water into a saucepan and add agar-agar.
- if rum and/or coconut water is not available, use the same amount of water instead

- Place the saucepan over medium heat and, stirring constantly, bring the mixture to a boil. Then add sugar and glucose or glucose and fructose syrup, mix. Increase the mixer speed.
- Keep stirring and bring the syrup to a boil. Cook until 108-110C. The finished syrup should run off the spatula in a continuous stream.

recipes.title: QUICHE LORRAINE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
with salmon, broccoli and gorgonzola

Russian version @ma_rusya_manko

I saw the recipe for this delicious pastry at Mary’s account @mary.s_kitchen_. An appetizing picture attracted me so much that I decided to bake it right away.

The quiche didn’t even cool down completely, as it disappeared from the plates! Therefore, if you have a desire to treat your loved ones with something incredibly tasty and yet easy to prepare, make use of this recipe.

Shortcrust base:
100 g of flour
70 g of whole grain flour
100 g of cold butter
2 tbsps of ice water
1 egg yolk
a pinch of salt

- Mix the dry ingredients. Add the cold diced butter and turn everything into a crumble with a mixer (with a paddle attachment) or chop it with a knife.
- Add the yolk, water and salt. As soon as the dough can be shaped into a ball, stop mixing it. Slightly roll out the dough, wrap it in plastic wrap and put in the fridge for 1-2 h.
- Roll out the dough into a layer 3-4 mm thick and put it in a mold d=18 cm, making the borders 4-5 cm high, prick with a fork and put it in the freezer for 10-15 min.
- Put a sheet of parchment paper on top of the dough in the mold and fill it with some weight (e.g. beans or lentils).
- Bake it in a preheated oven for 15 min with the weight on and 10 min without it, until the base is lightly browned.

### Filling
250 g of salmon fillet
200 g of broccoli
70 g of gorgonzola

- Dice the salmon, removing the pin bones. Crumble the cheese with your hands into small pieces.
- Disassemble the broccoli into separate inflorescences, cut large ones into pieces and cook them for 1-2 min in boiling salted water. Pour into a colander to drain.

Egg and sour cream mixture:
3 eggs
250 g of sour cream 15%
salt, pepper to taste *

- Mix all ingredients until homogeneous.
- Put the filling into the base, pour the egg and sour cream mixture on top. Bake at 200°C/392°F for about 40-50 min. The filling should set.
- Let the quiche cool down for 20 min.

* Be sure to taste your cheese before adding salt to the egg and sour cream mixture. If it's too salty, then don’t add salt to it.

recipes.title: SAN SEBASTIAN BASQUE BURNT CHEESECAKE RECIPE
recipes.docx:
Judging by your reaction to my stories I understood that not everyone has heard of this Spanish variation of a cheesecake, and, what is more, not everyone has tried it.

Your messages like "Can't you see that it burned down?!" clearly proved it. Those who didn't ask me such questions, probably thought the same, right?

I was enchanted by the simplicity of this recipe! A child's play – you put all the ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth, then pour into a mold and "burn" in the oven at maximum temperature.

But ... I had to remake it at least a dozen times till I finally achieved the desired result. As you can see, there were also some fine details and nuances.

The first cheesecake turned out to be like a curd cheese casserole, same thing happened to the second one. I changed the recipe. It turned out better, but still not perfect. I tediously had been choosing the baking mode, as well as the size of the cake ring.

In short, the whole point of this cheesecake is that it should be burnt on top, while remaining slightly underbaked on the inside.

Two worst pastry chef's nightmares legally settled in this recipe – a burnt crust and an underbaked centre.

Many of you DM me to buy the recipe, but I promised that I would publish the recipe for free. If I had known how much effort it would require, I would have reconsidered promising that. Just kidding. As you can see, the recipe is hard-won and torn from my heart. I hope you appreciate it and shower me with

### Ingredients

- 450 g of cream cheese
- 460 g of whipping cream 33-36%
- 150-200 g of sugar
- 240 g of whole eggs
- 30 g of cornstarch
- 1 tbsp. of vanilla paste

- Preheat oven to 230 °C / 446 °F with upper and lower heat mode on. Line an 18 cm cake ring with two parchment paper sheets.

- Put all the ingredients into a blender and process until smooth. Pour the mixture into the prepared mold.

- Bake the cheesecake until its top is burnt. In my oven it takes about 30 minutes. The ready cheesecake should jiggle very well in the center.

- Let the cheesecake cool down, then put it in the fridge overnight.

tips.title: FLAVOR INFUSION: WHAT, WITH WHAT, AND HOW
tips.docx:
Part 1

At first glance, this topic may seem very simple, as if there is not much to discuss. But! You might be surprised to learn that even when I was running a masterclass at a large-scale production facility, my recommendation to switch to cold aromatization came as a surprise to the team.

In reality, aroma and taste are inseparably connected and should always be considered as a whole.

Flavor–aroma pairing is a fascinating field you inevitably encounter when working in pastry arts. Once baking basic shortbread cookies or classic apple cakes is no longer inspiring, a natural desire arises to explore new or unconventional flavor combinations and to introduce subtle aromatic notes.

A well-chosen aroma and the dessert’s aftertaste can calm a person or, on the contrary, make them feel more energized; it can bring comfort or encourage reflection. For example, vanilla conveys warmth and a sense of calm, cinnamon evokes the feeling of a cozy autumn, while lemongrass and lavender have soothing properties.

To transfer aroma from one ingredient to another, they must be combined under specific conditions:

- mixed together (stirred or blended)
- chilled together
- heated together
- simmered together

What can be aromatized?
In mousses:

- the liquid base (cream / milk)
- the sugar syrup used for whipping egg whites (if the mousse is based on Italian meringue)
- mousses may also be aromatized using pastes

- Only thick pastes are used — those that do not compromise, but rather improve the dessert’s texture:
— nut pastes, praline paste, certain fruit pastes

In ganaches:

- fruit purée
- water

In berry fillings:

- the berries themselves or berry purée are aromatized using the cold method or through vacuum infusion
In sponge cakes and other baked goods exposed to high temperatures:
- the aromatizing ingredient is added directly to the recipe
Pt 2
In the previous part, we discussed WHAT can be flavored. Today, let’s talk about WHAT TO USE to do that.

Most likely, the first thing that comes to mind is flavorings. Both natural or nature-identical flavorings, as well as synthetic ones, can help add aroma to desserts.

This method has 3 obvious advantages:

1. it doesn’t require much time or effort — add a few drops, stir, and it’s done;

2. it helps in situations where you aren’t allowed to add extra ingredients in order not to change the texture;

3. it’s convenient when you need an unusual flavor (bubble gum, California strawberry, tiramisu).

In addition to flavorings, you can enhance the aroma of your desserts with:

- vanilla (pods / paste / extract)
- spices and seasonings (pepper, cinnamon, cardamom, anise, coriander, star anise, cloves, ginger)
- herbs and flowers (tarragon, basil, dill, thyme, rosemary, lavender)
- tea (black, matcha, red, green)
- fruit pastes
- citrus zest
- freeze-dried berries
- tonka beans
- coffee beans
- alcoholic beverages (rum, brandy, liqueurs, infusions)
- syrups
- natural essential extracts and oils

And this list is far from complete!

We’ve figured out WHAT to use. Now let’s talk about HOW to use it. There are several flavoring and infusion methods:

- cold infusion
- hot infusion
- flavoring by simmering
- vacuum sealing

tips.title: COLD INFUSION
tips.docx:
Cold infusion involves adding a specific flavoring component (spices, herbs, zest, etc.) to a liquid (cream, milk, berry purée) and then infusing it in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours.

This is the longest method — flavor develops slowly and is less intense than when using the hot infusion method.
To completely extract aroma from fresh herbs, you’ll need 3–5 days, and from dried ones — about 20 days.

Part 3

Continuing to explore the topic of flavor infusion, today we’ll look at the hot method, which I use quite often when developing recipes.

tips.title: THE HOT METHOD
tips.docx:
Many of you have probably already guessed that the hot method involves heat treatment—and you’re absolutely right.

Hot infusion means bringing a liquid to a boil together with spices, herbs, or other flavoring ingredients, and then letting it steep for 30–60 minutes.

You can use cream, milk, or berry purée as the base for infusion. For example, you can infuse cream with dried lavender flowers, as I did in the Blueberry–Lavender Cheesecake, or create a rich coffee aroma by infusing cream with ground coffee (the Coffee–Baileys Cheesecake).

It’s very simple. But there are a few secrets I’d love to share with you.

Many of you have probably already guessed that the hot method involves heat treatment—and you’re absolutely right.

tips.title: SECRETS OF THE HOT METHOD
tips.docx:
- Heat the liquid for infusion over medium or low heat so it warms up gradually.

- During the infusion process, try to use as little extra equipment as possible when preparing ingredients. For example, it’s better to zest citrus directly into the cream rather than onto a board first and then transferring it. Spices, herbs, and citrus contain a large amount of essential oils, which evaporate easily.

- Once the liquid reaches a boil, remove the saucepan from the heat immediately. At excessively high temperatures, flavoring ingredients may release compounds that negatively affect the taste and aroma.

- After heating, it’s best to cover the liquid with plastic wrap directly on the surface. If you use a lid, excess condensation may form and drip back into the liquid, and a film can develop on the surface that you’ll later have to remove.

- After the infusion time, strain the liquid through a sieve or cheesecloth.

- Once completely cooled, the infused liquid can be stored in the refrigerator for the same shelf life as the base product. However, keep in mind that the aroma will gradually fade with each day of storage.

tips.title: FACTORS THAT AFFECT STARCH FUNCTIONALITY
tips.docx:
In previous posts, we discussed different types of starch and how starch works. Today, let’s focus on what specifically affects the rate of starch thickening.

- So, the factors that influence the gelatinization temperature (t°) of starch include:

— TYPE OF STARCH — each type of starch has an optimal amount of heat required for proper gelatinization.

The time required for complete gelatinization of root starches is always shorter than that required for corn starch. In most cases, unmodified root starches should not be brought to a boil. When cooked for too long, unmodified root starches develop an excessively elastic or stringy texture.

— AMOUNT OF TENDERIZERS — sugars and fats slow down the rate at which starch granules absorb water and swell.

The slower they absorb water, the longer it takes for starch granules to gelatinize. In fact, if enough sugar is present, it can completely prevent starch gelatinization. This is one of the ways sugars and fats tenderize baked goods: they reduce the amount of gelatinized starch, which is responsible for structure formation. Sugar also increases the transparency of starch-thickened mixtures.

— AMOUNT OF ACID — acids hydrolyze (break down) large starch molecules into smaller ones, reducing their thickening power.

Acids also weaken starch granules, allowing them to gelatinize faster and more easily. In fact, if enough acid is present, gelatinization occurs so rapidly that the starch mixture may appear not to thicken at all.
STARCH. How does it work?

The process depends on the temperature setting. When starch granules are placed in cold water, its molecules attract water molecules and the granules swell just slightly. However, when the water is heated, the starch granules undergo an irreversible process called GELATINIZATION.

There is an optimal amount of heat for proper thickening and gel formation:

— too little heat → too few granules swell

— too much heat → too many granules break down

Undercooking or overcooking starch results in insufficient thickening and gel formation.

UNDERCOOKING starch causes additional problems as well:

— because raw granules are hard and dense, undercooked starch feels gritty in the mouth

— undercooked starch is opaque and has an unpleasant starch taste

— if stored for a day or longer, undercooked starch mixtures tend to release droplets or even pools of water around the gel

There are many factors affect the gelatinization t° of starches. The higher the gelatinization t°, the longer starch takes to gelatinize and, thus, the greater the risk of undercooking.

Here are the factors that affect starch gelatinization t°:

• type of starch used

• amount of fats and sugar

• amount of acid
